overall: Atlanta is warming steadily this morning with a running max of 78.8°F at 10:35 ET, consistent with a partly sunny June day. The 2-hour velocity is a solid +2.7°F/hr, but the 30-minute velocity has gone flat (0.0°F/hr) and acceleration is sharply negative at -2.7°F/hr², suggesting the warming pace may be stalling earlier than the model-predicted peak of ~14:36 ET. Cloud fraction remains elevated at 62% despite a FEW sky designation, which could act as a moderate cap on afternoon heating.
forecast_obs_notes: There is notable model disagreement today: HRRR (88.4°F) and NWS text (88°F) are bullish, while ECMWF (84.0°F) and NBM (84.6°F) are roughly 4°F cooler — a meaningful spread for a mid-summer day. Observed temps are tracking below where HRRR would expect by this hour, lending some credibility to the cooler ECMWF/NBM guidance. The active flood warnings are for far southeast Georgia rivers (Satilla River), not metro Atlanta, and have no meaningful impact on today's heating.
max_temp_prediction: With ~4 hours until the expected peak, the temperature needs to climb roughly 7-9°F from the current 78.8°F to reach NWS/HRRR targets — doable if warming resumes, but the stalled 30-minute velocity and negative acceleration are cautionary flags. The META model (most reliable) distributes probability broadly across 84–91°F, with 84-85F, 88-89F, and 90-91F each at ~21.6%, reflecting genuine uncertainty. For the active EVEN-bucket market, the 86-87°F bucket at 22.6% is the top pick and aligns well with a blend of cooler model guidance (ECMWF/NBM ~84-85°F) and warmer guidance (HRRR/NWS ~88°F); moderate confidence in the 86-88°F range.
